prompt: Explain how U.S. health insurance works using only fantasy football metaphors.
response:
Welcome to the **U.S. Health Insurance Fantasy League**, where managing your roster is high-stakes and the waiver wire is your primary care physician. Here is how the system works, translated entirely into fantasy football terms.

### The Draft (Open Enrollment)
You cannot just add players to your roster whenever you want. You have a strict **Draft Window** (Open Enrollment Period). During this time, you must select your "Team" (Insurance Plan). If you miss the draft, you are stuck with an empty bench for the rest of the season unless you experience a **Roster-Changing Life Event** (marriage, birth, job loss), which triggers a special waiver period.

### Salary Cap and Roster Construction (Premiums)
Every week, you pay a **Salary Cap Hit** (Premium) just to keep your team active in the league. This cost is deducted from your bankroll regardless of whether your players actually play that week. You can’t skip payments because your star RB didn't touch the ball; you still have to pay the cap hit to remain eligible.

### The Flex Spot (Deductible)
Before your elite players start scoring points for you, you have to burn through your **Flex Threshold** (Deductible). This is the amount of yardage you must gain out of your own pocket before the league starts contributing to your score.
*   **High Flex Threshold (High Deductible Plan):** Lower weekly salary cap hit, but you’re carrying the load solo for the first 1,000 yards of the season.
*   **Low Flex Threshold (Low Deductible Plan):** Higher weekly salary cap hit, but the league starts helping you score much earlier in the drive.

### Points Per Reception (Copays and Coinsurance)
Once you clear the Flex Threshold, the league starts scoring with you, but not at 100% efficiency.
*   **Copay:** A fixed PPR bonus. Every time you visit a specialist (start a specific player), you pay a flat 5-point fee, and the league covers the rest of that player’s stat line.
*   **Coinsurance:** A percentage-based split. For expensive procedures (big-play touchdowns), you might split the production 80/20. You get credit for 80% of the yards; the other 20% comes out of your personal stats.

### The Playoff Ceiling (Out-of-Pocket Maximum)
This is the most critical stat in the league. It is the absolute maximum number of negative points you can absorb in a single season. Once your personal losses hit this **Playoff Ceiling**, the league takes over completely and covers 100% of all remaining roster moves, injuries, and stat corrections for the rest of the year. It is your hard floor against total season collapse.

### League Formats (HMO vs. PPO)
*   **HMO (Redraft League):** You can *only* start players on your official roster (In-Network). If you try to start a free agent or a player from another league (Out-of-Network), their stats count for **zero**. Also, you must consult your Team Captain (PCP) for permission before activating any specialist players.
*   **PPO (Dynasty/Deeper League):** You have a preferred roster that scores maximum points, but you are allowed to start outside players (Out-of-Network) at a reduced scoring rate. You don’t need your Team Captain’s sign-off to make moves, giving you more flexibility but requiring more active management.

### The Commissioner’s Veto (Prior Authorization)
Even if a player is on your roster and healthy, the **League Commissioner** (Insurer) can veto your starting lineup. Before certain high-value plays (specialist visits, surgeries, brand-name meds), you must submit a transaction request. If the Commissioner deems the move "not medically necessary" or "out of protocol," the play is nullified, and you get zero points for that week despite having the player available.

### Free Agency (Out-of-Network Care)
In this league, free agents are wildly expensive. Using an out-of-network facility is like starting a player who isn't even in your league's database; the scoring system may not recognize them at all, leaving you to absorb the full, unadjusted stat line against your salary cap. Always check your league’s official depth chart (Provider Directory) before kickoff.
